claims: The Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is currently carrying four astronauts—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen—on a 10-day trip around the Moon and back.
The Artemis II mission crew is in orbit.
The Artemis II mission spacecraft is performing as expected following successful separation from the rocket.
The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight to the Moon since 1972.
The Artemis II mission is the first to fly beyond low-Earth orbit in over five decades.
The Artemis II mission lasts 10 days.
The Artemis II mission is aimed at testing critical systems for future moon landings.
The Artemis II mission includes three Americans and one Canadian.
The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight of the Artemis program.
